speaker: ophelia
text: Ophelia Stroud. I run the {city} branch. Well, I’ve been running it; nobody actually asked me to. We’ve tripled since spring. I’d like a seat at the table.

choices.label: Welcome to the table, Regional Director.
choices.reaction: Ophelia sits down at the table and, within a minute, is somehow at the head of it.

effects.memory: Ophelia Stroud, who built the {city} branch, became Regional Director.

choices.label: Branches report to {hq}. That’s how it works.
choices.reaction: “Of course,” says Ophelia, in a voice that files the remark somewhere safe.

speaker: lionel
text: Lionel Fitch. I came to observe. I’ve now observed. You have no structure. You have a garage, a soup committee and a lot of goodwill. I propose seven departments.

choices.label: Seven departments it is.
choices.reaction: By Friday there are seven departments, each with a logo. The logos are surprisingly good.

effects.memory: Lionel Fitch reorganized {movement} into seven departments.

choices.label: We’ll grow our own way.
choices.reaction: Lionel nods and stays anyway, taking notes in a small leather notebook marked OBSERVATIONS.

speaker: martin
text: Lionel has replaced my laminated sign with a laminated policy about laminated signs. I founded this with you. Who decides how things are run now: me, or him?

choices.label: You do, Martin.
choices.hint: Loyalty to a founder · Lionel sidelined
choices.reaction: Martin rehangs his sign. It is slightly crooked, which he decides to leave as a statement.

choices.label: Lionel does. It’s his job now.
choices.reaction: Martin says he understands. He goes home and laminates nothing for the first time in years.

speaker: martin
text: Do you remember the first gathering? Seven people. Four thought it was a book club. I knew every name. I don’t know anyone’s name any more, {title}.

choices.label: Then help me fix that. Run the founders’ council.
choices.reaction: The founders’ council meets in Gary’s garage, for old times’ sake. Martin brings name tags.

choices.label: That’s what growing looks like.
choices.reaction: Martin agrees that it is. He starts arriving late, then leaving early.

speaker: lionel
text: The Department of Refreshments has requested budget to form a Department of Cookies. The Department of Cookies has, in turn, requested a Deputy.
variants: The Department of Refreshments has requested budget to form a Department of Cookies. The Department of Cookies has, in turn, requested a Deputy.
Form 14-B, the form for requesting Form 14-A, now has a waiting list. I propose a Form 14-C to manage the list.
Two departments have discovered they are doing the same job. Both would like the other one abolished.

choices.label: Approve it. Process is important.
choices.reaction: Approved. The approval itself requires approval, which arrives the following week.

choices.label: Merge the departments.
choices.reaction: The departments merge. Their logos merge too, into something that looks like a confused owl.

speaker: agenda:expansion
text: The {city} branch does “{tradition}” differently. They say it suits them better. {hometown} says it’s heresy. {city} says {hometown} says everything is heresy.

choices.label: Let {city} have its local version.
choices.reaction: The {city} version spreads to two neighboring towns within a month. Nobody can say which is the original any more.

choices.label: One movement, one way.
choices.reaction: {city} complies. Its {meeting} becomes very correct and noticeably quieter.

speaker: ophelia
text: I have a plan to reach every town within a day’s drive by spring. It needs organizers, a budget and, frankly, fewer decisions going through {hq}.

choices.label: Do it. You have my backing.
choices.reaction: Ophelia’s plan arrives as a forty-page document with a map, a timeline and your signature already on it.

choices.label: Slower, and through {hq}.
choices.reaction: Ophelia revises the plan. The new version is two pages long and says “as directed” eleven times.

speaker: ophelia
text: The branches are asking who actually leads {movement}. Some of them have started saying it’s me. I haven’t discouraged them. I think we should discuss what happens next.

choices.label: Share leadership with Ophelia.
choices.reaction: A joint statement is issued. It is mostly in Ophelia’s handwriting.

effects.memory: {title} agreed to share the leadership of {movement} with Ophelia Stroud.

choices.label: There is one leader.
choices.reaction: Ophelia smiles, thanks you for your clarity, and calls a meeting of the branch leaders. You are not invited.

speaker: ophelia
text: Several branches have voted to become independent. They’ll keep the customs, the name with a small amendment, and me. We can part as friends, or not.

choices.label: Part as friends.
choices.reaction: {movement} (Regional) is founded the next day. They send flowers. The card is signed by Ophelia and four hundred others.

effects.memory: Ophelia Stroud led several branches out of {movement} to form {movement} (Regional).

choices.label: Fight for every branch.
choices.reaction: It is a long, ugly month of competing {meetings}. You keep most of the branches and lose most of your sleep.

speaker: any
text: Agnes’s Original {movement} has opened a branch in {city}. Their leaflet says we have “lost the minutes, and with them our way.”

choices.label: Invite Agnes to talks.
choices.reaction: Agnes attends. She brings the original minutes and reads from them for two hours. Some of it is genuinely moving.

choices.label: Out-recruit them.
choices.reaction: Two rival {meetings} on the same street, on the same night. Both are well attended. Neither will admit it.

speaker: any
text: Rolf has launched a company. It sells our customs as a monthly subscription box, with an app. It is doing extremely well.

choices.label: Denounce it publicly.
choices.reaction: The denunciation is shared widely, mostly by people who then buy the box out of curiosity.

choices.label: Negotiate a licensing deal.
choices.reaction: Rolf answers the phone on the first ring, as if he had been waiting. He had.

speaker: gary
text: There are people outside my garage. From other towns. They want to see where it started. One of them asked if they could touch the lawnmower.

choices.label: Open the garage to visitors.
choices.hint: Tradition · Gary becomes a tour guide
choices.reaction: Gary gives tours. He is wonderful at it, mostly because he gets the history slightly wrong in a way everyone prefers.

effects.memory: Gary’s garage became a place of pilgrimage.

choices.label: Ask them to respect Gary’s privacy.
choices.reaction: The visitors leave politely. One leaves a small plaque on the gate. Gary keeps it polished.

speaker: priya
text: A publisher wants a cookbook. “The Soups of {movement}.” They want me to write it, and they want you to write the foreword.

choices.label: Write the foreword.
choices.reaction: Your foreword is two pages about the night soup became a thing. Priya cries at the launch, into a soup.

choices.label: Soup shouldn’t be a product.
choices.reaction: Priya agrees, sadly, and writes it anyway as a pamphlet. It is photocopied eight thousand times.

speaker: dez
text: Hear me out. Highway billboard. Forty feet wide. Your face, the word {movement}, and the phrase “Obviously.” I’ve put down a deposit.

choices.label: Put my face on the highway.
choices.reaction: The billboard causes a minor traffic incident and a major surge in enquiries. Your face is now a landmark.

choices.label: Get the deposit back.
choices.reaction: Dez gets half the deposit back and spends it on a slightly smaller billboard, of his own face.

text: Gatherings of over two hundred people now require a permit. Your {meetings} have been very large. Some of them were, technically, parades.

choices.label: Apply for the permits.
choices.reaction: The permits arrive. Lionel, or someone very like him, frames the first one.

choices.label: Smaller {meetings}, more of them.
choices.reaction: Forty small {meetings} spring up in living rooms across the region. It feels, people say, like the garage days.

text: Half my constituents seem to be {members}, and the other half want to know why. I’m up for re-election. Would {movement} endorse me?

choices.label: Endorse the mayor.
choices.reaction: The mayor wins comfortably and starts every speech with {belief}. Some members love it. Some feel used.

choices.label: We don’t do politics.
choices.reaction: The mayor is disappointed but impressed. She attends a {meeting} anyway, as a private citizen with a large entourage.

speaker: agenda:expansion
text: Regional radio has offered us a weekly show. Thirty minutes, Sunday mornings. The producer asked who our “voice” is. Everyone looked at you.

choices.label: I’ll host it myself.
choices.reaction: Your first broadcast is twenty-nine minutes of nerves and one minute of something genuinely good. Listeners write in about that minute.

choices.label: Let the members host it.
choices.reaction: A different member hosts every week. The week Gary hosts is the most popular episode by a distance.

speaker: agenda:order
text: The official newsletter needs an editorial line. Some want news. Some want doctrine. Gary has submitted a nine-page piece about whales.

choices.label: News and doctrine, plus Gary’s whales.
choices.reaction: The newsletter triples in length. The whale section is the most read.

choices.label: Doctrine only.
choices.reaction: The newsletter becomes four pages of carefully checked doctrine. It is cited often and read rarely.

text: We’d like to propose “{movement} Lite.” All the community, none of the mandatory anything. People would join who never would otherwise.

choices.label: Allow a lighter membership.
choices.reaction: Lite membership is enormously popular. The traditionalists refer to Lite members exclusively as “tourists.”

effects.memory: {movement} introduced a lighter form of membership.

choices.label: Membership means something.
choices.reaction: The proposal is declined. The reformers start meeting on a different night, “just to talk.”

text: The Knitting Circle now has branches in nine towns. It turns out a common enemy is very good for recruitment. We thought you should know. That’s all.

choices.label: Propose a truce. And a joint event.
choices.reaction: The joint event is a craft fair with soup. It is the most peaceful afternoon either organization has ever had.

choices.label: This is war.
choices.reaction: Both organizations recruit furiously. Wool sales and {movement} membership rise together.

speaker: lionel
text: I’ve reviewed the founding decisions. Some of them are, with respect, not scalable. “{belief}” for example. Have you considered a pilot program?

choices.label: Our founding customs are not up for review.
choices.reaction: Lionel writes “not up for review” in his notebook and underlines it, which is his version of shouting.

choices.label: Run the pilot.
choices.reaction: The pilot program for {belief} has a steering group, three phases and a launch event. It is, somehow, still {belief}.

speaker: dez
text: Small thing. I may have promised the {city} branch that {title} would visit. Personally. Every week. Forever.

choices.label: Keep the promise, for a while.
choices.reaction: You visit {city} every week for two months. They name a bench after you. Dez takes the credit.

choices.label: Correct the promise.
choices.reaction: {city} accepts a monthly visit instead, and a signed photograph that Dez had already printed.

speaker: any
text: National television wants a documentary. They’ve asked to film a {meeting}, the garage and you. Someone has to decide what kind of movement the country sees.

choices.label: Show them everything, as it is.
choices.reaction: The documentary shows Gary asleep, Martin’s laminated signs and a very large pot of something. The country falls a little bit in love.

effects.memory: {Movement} appeared on national television, exactly as it was.

choices.label: Show them the best version of us.
choices.reaction: The documentary is beautifully shot and slightly untrue. Nobody can quite say which parts.

effects.memory: {Movement} appeared on national television, at its very best.
